The Biscuit Supplier’s Recall Has No Public Notice, and This Is the Company Whose Sandwiches Hospitalized Ten People and Killed One Last Year. 
 Fresh & Ready Foods Recalls 2,414 Listeria-Risk Biscuit Sandwiches From Washington and Oregon Break Rooms and Vending Machines. The Biscuit Supplier’s Recall Has No Public Notice, and This Is the Company Whose Sandwiches Hospitalized Ten People and Killed One Last Year.
 By Bill Marler on November 9, 2026 
 Posted in Food Poisoning Information 
 Fresh & Ready Foods LLC of Renton, Washington,  recalled 2,414 Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwiches  on November 7, 2026, for possible  Listeria monocytogenes , after its biscuit supplier, C.H. Guenther & Son, recalled the biscuits baked into them. The sandwiches went to employee break rooms, refrigerated vending machines and cafeterias in Washington and Oregon between October 25 and November 4, carry Fresh Thru dates of 11/07 through 11/19, and as of November 9 no illnesses have been reported. FDA posted the notice on Sunday, November 8.
 The recall covers one sandwich, one plant and two states. 
 The product is a 4.6-ounce sandwich in clear plastic film, SKU 3100048, UPC 8 405493 0168 4, made at the company’s Renton facility. Fresh & Ready says the recalled biscuit went into this sandwich and nothing else, and that no other Fresh To You or Fresh & Ready product, production date or facility is affected. Consumers are told not to eat it, to throw it out, and to call 1-855-424-8390 weekdays between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. Eastern for a refund. The notice names no employer, no vending operator and no cafeteria.
 Date What happened Days from first shipment 
 October 25, 2026 First recalled sandwiches shipped to Washington and Oregon break rooms, vending and cafeterias 0 
 November 4, 2026 Last recalled sandwiches shipped 10 
 November 7, 2026 Fresh & Ready Foods issues the recall after the C.H. Guenther & Son biscuit recall 13 
 November 8, 2026 FDA posts the company announcement 14 
 November 19, 2026 Last Fresh Thru date on recalled product 25 
 Source: Fresh & Ready Foods company announcement as posted by FDA, November 8, 2026, read November 9, 2026. Check: October has 31 days, so October 25 to November 7 is 6 + 7 = 13 days, and October 25 to November 19 is 6 + 19 = 25 days. The table is my arithmetic, not FDA’s. 
 The supplier’s recall is the one you cannot read. 
 Fresh & Ready’s notice exists because C.H. Guenther & Son, a Texas baking company, recalled “certain biscuit products” for possible  Listeria monocytogenes . As of this morning there is no C.H. Guenther & Son entry on  FDA’s recall page , no company press release I could find, and nothing in the enforcement report, which has not yet published the event. A biscuit baked for one sandwich maker in Renton was almost certainly baked for other customers. Who they are, what they put the biscuits into, and whether their products are still in a cooler somewhere is not public.
 This is the problem I wrote about in October when  FDA knew the supplier behind fifty  E. coli  illnesses and would not say its name . A recall that is never posted protects the supplier’s customer list and no one else. FDA has had  final guidance since November 2020 permitting it to publish retail consignee lists  when a recalled food is not easily identified on the shelf. A biscuit inside somebody else’s sandwich is the definition of not easily identified. Nothing in the guidance stops FDA from posting the Guenther notice and the list of who received the biscuits. It should.
 Vending machines and break rooms have no customer-service desk. 
 Most recalls reach people through a store: a register sign, a shelf tag, a loyalty-card email. A sandwich bought from a vending machine or a break room on October 28 has none of that. The person who ate it does not know the vending operator’s name, the operator may not know which machine took which lot, and the employer is not in the food business at all. No illnesses have been reported, which is good news with an asterisk:  Listeria can take up to 70 days to make someone sick, so the reporting window on sandwiches sold through November 4 runs into January. If you are an employer or a vending operator in Washington or Oregon who received these sandwiches, telling your people is on you, because no one else can.
 Fresh & Ready Foods’ last  Listeria  problem took a year to find and killed someone. 
 In May 2025 I wrote that  a  Listeria  outbreak had hit ten people in California and Nevada , all ten hospitalized. CDC had opened the investigation in 2024, could not find the food, and closed it. The break came on March 31, 2025, when FDA swabbed the Fresh & Ready Foods plant in San Fernando, California, and whole genome sequencing tied the environmental isolates to the sick. Records showed the company’s ready-to-eat foods had been served in at least three healthcare facilities where patients later fell ill. On May 10, 2025, the company recalled sandwiches, snacks and pasta under the Fresh & Ready Foods, City Point Market Fresh Food to Go and Fresh Take Crave Away brands, sold to hospitals, hotels, convenience stores, airports and airlines in Arizona, California, Nevada and Washington.  FDA’s final page  counts 10 sick, 10 hospitalized and one death, in Nevada. Food Poison Journal carried  the death when FDA recorded it .
 FDA addressed the warning letter to Compass Group USA. 
 The  September 5, 2025 warning letter  about the San Fernando plant was not sent to Fresh & Ready Foods. It went to Tim Lonc, President of Compass Group USA, in Charlotte, North Carolina. It records  Listeria monocytogenes  on a conveyor belt and roller where in-process sandwiches were placed and on a slicer plate; positives in 2017, including a food-contact mixing bowl;  Listeria innocua  in 2011, 2017 and 2018; and a hazard analysis that did not treat environmental pathogens as a hazard requiring a preventive control. Clinical isolates from California and Nevada matched two of the 2025 swabs.  I posted the letter in full  in November 2025. FDA, in other words, treated the sandwich plant as the responsibility of one of the largest food service companies in the country. The Renton plant recalling sandwiches this week belongs to the same Fresh & Ready Foods LLC.
 What is different this time, and what is not. 
 Fairness requires saying what is different. The 2025 outbreak came from  Listeria  living inside the company’s own plant for years. The 2026 recall, on the company’s account, came from a supplier’s biscuit, at a different plant, and Fresh & Ready pulled the product within three days of its last shipment and before anyone was reported sick. That is how a recall is supposed to work. What has not changed is the structure around it. A supplier recall is still invisible to the public. A food service recall still reaches the eater last, if at all. And a company that FDA found had  Listeria  on food-contact surfaces across eight years still does not have to tell its vending customers anything beyond a notice on a government website posted on a Sunday. I have represented people made sick by  Listeria  for more than thirty years, including the families of all 33 people who died in the 2011 Jensen Farms cantaloupe outbreak, and the pattern that keeps the phone ringing is not the exotic failure. It is the ordinary one that no one was assigned to tell anyone about.
 What Washington and Oregon workers should do. 
 If you bought a Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich from a break room, vending machine or cafeteria since October 25, check the Fresh Thru date on the front label. Dates from 11/07 through 11/19 are recalled. Do not eat it. If you already ate one and you are pregnant, over 65 or have a weakened immune system, tell your doctor now and watch for fever, muscle aches, headache, stiff neck or confusion for the next two months. CDC says invasive illness usually starts within two weeks, but it can take far longer. The consumer version of this recall, with symptoms and what to ask a doctor, is on  Food Poison Journal , which has followed this company since the 2025 recall.
 Which Fresh & Ready sandwich is recalled for  Listeria ? 
 One product: Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich, 4.6 oz, SKU 3100048, UPC 8 405493 0168 4, Fresh Thru dates 11/07 through 11/19, sold in Washington and Oregon break rooms, refrigerated vending machines and cafeterias between October 25 and November 4, 2026.
 Has anyone gotten sick from the recalled biscuit sandwiches? 
 No illnesses had been reported as of November 9, 2026.  Listeria  symptoms can take up to 70 days to appear, so that can change.
 Why was the biscuit recalled in the first place? 
 Fresh & Ready says its supplier, C.H. Guenther & Son, recalled certain biscuit products for possible  Listeria monocytogenes . That supplier recall has no public notice on FDA’s recall page as of November 9, so the reason, the test result and the other customers are not public.
